issues.title: Static IS_DEV check in GeneralUtils throws outside a Fabric launch (plain unit tests)
issues.body:
Hi, and thanks for this and the other server-side mods, really appreciated!

## Context

I'm writing a server-side Fabric side-mod for [Cobblemon](https://cobblemon.com/), so we are on Minecraft 1.21.1 and bundle `eu.pb4:placeholder-api:2.4.2+1.21` (Mojang mappings, Architectury Loom). I'm unit-testing our message formatting with plain JUnit 5. The game isn't launched in these tests, so there is no Fabric launcher.

## Problem

The first parse or `toText` call loads `GeneralUtils`, because `ParentNode` uses `GeneralUtils.CASTER` and `GeneralUtils.isEmpty` ([ParentNode.java#L22](https://github.com/Patbox/TextPlaceholderAPI/blob/2427627df3e73ec00a2d3623c7e60e1d076bdb67/src/main/java/eu/pb4/placeholders/api/node/parent/ParentNode.java#L22), [#L43](https://github.com/Patbox/TextPlaceholderAPI/blob/2427627df3e73ec00a2d3623c7e60e1d076bdb67/src/main/java/eu/pb4/placeholders/api/node/parent/ParentNode.java#L43)). Its static initializer runs [`IS_DEV = FabricLoader.getInstance().isDevelopmentEnvironment()`](https://github.com/Patbox/TextPlaceholderAPI/blob/2427627df3e73ec00a2d3623c7e60e1d076bdb67/src/main/java/eu/pb4/placeholders/impl/GeneralUtils.java#L21), which calls `FabricLauncherBase.getLauncher().isDevelopment()`. With no launcher this fails with `ExceptionInInitializerError` caused by:

    NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "net.fabricmc.loader.impl.launch.FabricLauncher.isDevelopment()" because the return value of "net.fabricmc.loader.impl.launch.FabricLauncherBase.getLauncher()" is null

After that, `GeneralUtils` can't be initialized, so every later parse of a tag in the same JVM fails with `NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class eu.pb4.placeholders.impl.GeneralUtils`.

## Why it matters

As far as I can tell, `IS_DEV` has a single use: [`PlaceholderNode.java#L27`](https://github.com/Patbox/TextPlaceholderAPI/blob/2427627df3e73ec00a2d3623c7e60e1d076bdb67/src/main/java/eu/pb4/placeholders/impl/placeholder/PlaceholderNode.java#L27), where it only gates the dev-only "Missing context for placeholders requiring them" log. Yet it makes parsing unusable outside a running game.

`main` (3.x) has the same pattern: [`LoaderUtil.IS_DEV`](https://github.com/Patbox/TextPlaceholderAPI/blob/718da0f9d2d6f6e8d6947c67f73f5cdaf01c9e6c/src/main/java/eu/pb4/placeholders/impl/LoaderUtil.java#L7) feeds [`GeneralUtils.IS_DEV`](https://github.com/Patbox/TextPlaceholderAPI/blob/718da0f9d2d6f6e8d6947c67f73f5cdaf01c9e6c/src/main/java/eu/pb4/placeholders/impl/GeneralUtils.java#L34), and it is still used only in [`PlaceholderNode`](https://github.com/Patbox/TextPlaceholderAPI/blob/718da0f9d2d6f6e8d6947c67f73f5cdaf01c9e6c/src/main/java/eu/pb4/placeholders/impl/placeholder/PlaceholderNode.java#L25). I haven't run 3.x myself.

I tried `fabric-loader-junit`, but its Knot classloader breaks `kotlin.test`'s `ServiceLoader` lookup and JDBC driver loading in our test suite. My current workaround installs a proxy `FabricLauncher` through `FabricLauncherBase.setLauncher`, which relies on Loader internals.

## Minimal reproduction

With `placeholder-api` and Fabric Loader on the test classpath, and no Fabric launcher running (plain JUnit 5):

    import eu.pb4.placeholders.api.parsers.NodeParser
    import net.minecraft.ChatFormatting
    import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals
    import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test

    class PlaceholderParsingTest {
        @Test
        fun parsesQuickTextTag() {
            val parser = NodeParser.builder().quickText().build()

            val text = parser.parseNode("<red>hi</red>").toText()

            assertEquals("hi", text.string)
            assertEquals(ChatFormatting.RED.color, text.siblings.single().style.color?.value)
        }
    }

Expected: the test passes. Actual: the first call fails with the `ExceptionInInitializerError` above and the assertions are never reached; any later parse of a tag in the same JVM fails with `NoClassDefFoundError`. Plain text without tags is unaffected.

(`net.minecraft.ChatFormatting` is the Mojang-mapped name; it is `Formatting` under Yarn.)

## Suggestion

Only a suggestion, since you know the codebase better. The flag could be read lazily at the log site, or guarded, for example by treating a missing launcher as "not development" (or "development", if you wish) or by catching the exception. That would keep the log behaviour in real dev environments and make parsing usable in plain unit tests.

Since Cobblemon is on 1.21.1, we can't move to 3.x, so would a fix also be possible on the 1.21.1 (2.4.x) line? I'm happy to open a PR if you'd like one.

issues.title: player:statistic doesn't work properly
issues.body:
I want to use the fish caught statistic in text. For that, I'm just writing `%player:statistic fish_caught%`.
However, that returns "Invalid statistic", despite it being valid. I also tried `minecraft:fish_caught`, but it was the same.

I looked in the code, and noticed the following:

`ctx.player().getStatHandler().getStat(Stats.CUSTOM.getOrCreateStat(Identifier.tryParse("minecraft:fish_caught")))` this doesn't work, but it's basically what placeholder api does.

`ctx.player().getStatHandler().getStat(Stats.CUSTOM.getOrCreateStat(Stats.FISH_CAUGHT))` this DOES work, despite it being an identifier, containing "minecraft:fish_caught"...

This is because stats are stored in an IdentityHashMap, which use reference equality. You can't make a new identifier and pass it in.

A fix would be, instead of doing `getOrCreateStat(identifier)`, do `getOrCreateStat(Registry.CUSTOM_STAT.get(identifier))`. I haven't tested, but this seems to fix the issue.

issues.title: Does not properly inject placeholders into minimessage style tags, like `<click>` or `<hover>`
issues.body:
Placeholders are not properly being injected into minimessage style tags like `<click>` or `<hover>`.

Example:
Using [styled chat](https://modrinth.com/mod/styled-chat) and [player pronouns](https://modrinth.com/mod/player-pronouns), I have the following configs set in for styled chat:

```json
{
  ...
  "defaultStyle": {
    "displayName": "%luckperms:prefix_element highest% <click:suggest_command:'/msg %player:name_unformatted%'><hover:show_text:'%playerpronouns:pronouns%'>${default}</hover></click>",
    "chat": "<click:suggest_command:'/msg %player:name_unformatted%'><hover:show_text:'%playerpronouns:pronouns%'><gray>%player:displayname_visual%<reset> <dark_gray>»</dark_gray><reset> ${message}",
    ...
  },
  ...
}
```

However, the hover action only displays the following for the hover action:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46940694/191574034-0649e66e-34ed-4806-90e8-abb5350f7490.png)

And, clicking on the message types the following: (note: the space at the end of `/msg`)
```
/msg 
```

However, changing out `<click:suggest_command:'/msg %player:name_unformatted%'>` for `<click:suggest_command:'/msg testing 123'>` inputs the following text:
```
/msg test 123
```


It seems that sometimes they're either being replaced with an empty string, or are not being replaced at all. I'm assuming this is a bug with the placeholder api, not minimessage.

issues.title: Returning incorrect name with %player:displayname_visual%
issues.body:
Currently, the placeholder api is returning the incorrect name with `%player:displayname_visual%`.

Example:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46940694/191571954-3afcd22a-6e37-4846-8e7b-6dc8c3cf603b.png)

It should be displaying

> *solo » [message here]

However, for some reason it is repeating the name twice (or more sometimes):
> *solo *solosolo » [message here]

You can compound the effect when nesting `%player:displayname_visual%`.

Using the [styled chat](https://modrinth.com/mod/styled-chat) mod, if you set `displayName` to something that includes `%player:displayname_visual%`, then you may get an output similar to the following:
> *solosolo *solosolosolosolo » [message here]


The mods 
- [styled nicknames](https://modrinth.com/mod/styled-nicknames)
- [styled chat](https://modrinth.com/mod/styled-chat)
are being used to customize the chat.


Here is a shortened version of my styled chat config to include all relevant info:

issues.title: Not reporting TPS correctly in combination with other mods which consume large amounts of CPU without affecting TPS
issues.body:
The default placeholders for the TPS is not reporting the correct values.

Reproducing:
1. Install the following mods:
  - [Styled Player List](https://modrinth.com/mod/styledplayerlist)
  - [Chunky Pregenerator](https://modrinth.com/mod/chunky)
  - [TabTPS](https://modrinth.com/mod/tabtps)
2. Configure player list to show both the TPS.
3. Execute `/tabtps toggle actionbar` to display actual tps on the action bar.
4. Start chunky pregenerator.
5. Watch TPS


Displayed TPS is incorrect:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46940694/156944692-20e5c992-81bd-44ca-84ca-8da580515c69.png)
Correct TPS:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46940694/156944700-749cfcad-44b7-4407-abc9-45a10a6e1f7d.png)

During both screenshots, a chunky pregeneration task is being executed, which consumes the server's CPU for generating chunks. The low tps of about 5 is also observed in game.

issues.title: Conditional placeholders
issues.body:
An option for conditional placeholders. For example, with the pronouns mod you could have the placeholder displayed like this:
```
if %playerpronouns:pronouns% != "Unknown" then
  display " (%playerpronouns:pronouns%)"
else
  display ""
end
```
The way I suggest implementing this is in a config file, a server owner could specify these conditions and give the conditions an ID. This ID could then be used in a placeholder.
